total_quotient_ring.new_proposed_wording:
For a finite birational normalization $A\subset B$, let $Q(A)$
be the total quotient ring obtained by inverting the non-zero-divisors
of $A$. Then $B\otimes_A Q(A)=Q(A)$. Every $A$-linear map
$\varphi:B\to A$ extends to a $Q(A)$-linear endomorphism of this
common total quotient ring, hence to multiplication by $\varphi(1)$.
Thus evaluation at $1$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,A)$ with
$\{a\in A:aB\subset A\}$. Finite duality therefore gives
total_quotient_ring.local_branch_model: A=C{x,y,z}/(xy) maps to B=C{x,z}⊕C{y,z} by a↦(a(x,0,z),a(0,y,z)). Localization by the non-zero-divisors identifies Q(A)=Frac(C{x,z})×Frac(C{y,z}), and the multiplication map B⊗_A Q(A)→Q(A) is an isomorphism.
total_quotient_ring.conductor_map: Every A-linear φ:B→A localizes to a Q(A)-linear map Q(A)→Q(A); it is multiplication by c=φ(1)∈A. Its values lie in A exactly when cB⊂A. Conversely multiplication by each such c is A-linear B→A. Evaluation at 1 and multiplication are inverse maps, giving Hom_A(B,A)≅{c∈A:cB⊂A}.
total_quotient_ring.frozen_wording_precision: The frozen phrase common total fraction field in §2 denotes the total quotient ring Q(A), which is the product of the branch fraction fields. At a point of normal N its local ring is a domain, so the later reflexive-ideal argument uses that local domain fraction field. The frozen bytes remain unchanged.
